oracle.endpoint_local_exhaustive_truth: pass for natural, two-arm final, exhaustive challenger best, v1 output, historical-v0 output, fixed64 output, and fixed128 output in all 40 cases

interpretation.primary: The preregistered v1 incumbent-preserving sequential challenger passed its usefulness rule on untouched n=16 transfer: it recovered 33/43 = 76.74% of exhaustive seeded-challenger quality gain while spending 4829/18314 = 26.37% of exhaustive challenger compilations, with zero per-case harm relative to the two-arm incumbent.
interpretation.fixed_prefix: At similar or greater compute, fixed128 recovered only 1/43 gain with 5118 compilations. Fixed64 recovered zero with 2600. Thus the v1 trajectory-conditioned continuation substantially outperformed uniform fixed-prefix allocation on this holdout.
interpretation.historical_v0: The failed v0 architecture recovered only 4/43 gain at 9.05% exhaustive compute. Removing the initial rejection and finishing a selected promising challenger materially increased recovery, but at higher compute.
interpretation.failure_scope: Two exhaustive benefits remained undetected because their gap after 64 stayed large (20 and 46) despite eventual late improvements at indices 247 and 336. The 64-prefix gap is therefore not a certificate of no future benefit and must remain a heuristic VoC signal, not a hard negative proof.
interpretation.scope: Synthetic positive-monotone graph 2-CNF ROBDD ordering only. This validates one allocation architecture under this search contract; it does not establish a general theorem-proving controller.
